title: A box already ticked
topic: Probity in records, forms and certification
stem:
You are an F2 doctor on the postnatal ward. Writing the discharge summary for Mrs Lee, who had a caesarean section two days ago, you notice that the template has automatically filled in "VTE risk assessment completed".

You haven't done a VTE assessment for her, and you can't find one in her notes.
instruction: Rank in order the following actions in response to this situation (1 = Most appropriate; 5 = Least appropriate).

options.text: Correct the summary so it reflects what was actually done.
options.detailed: Whatever the template says, the summary should only state what was done. Correcting it keeps the record honest.

options.text: Leave the entry, as the midwives usually assess VTE risk.
options.brief: You've checked and can't find an assessment.
options.detailed: Midwives may assess VTE risk in some units, but you've looked and found no record. Leaving the entry keeps a probably false statement and leaves her unassessed. It is the least appropriate option.

options.text: Complete her VTE risk assessment before she goes home.
options.brief: She may need thromboprophylaxis after a caesarean.
options.detailed: Women are at increased risk of blood clots after a caesarean section, and some need preventive treatment after discharge. Doing the assessment now protects her.

options.text: Report the template problem so it can be fixed.
options.brief: Other summaries may contain the same false statement.
options.detailed: If the template auto-fills this line, other women's summaries may say an assessment was done when it wasn't. Reporting it protects them.

options.text: Delete the line without doing the assessment.
options.brief: Removes the false statement but leaves her unassessed.
options.detailed: This makes the record honest, but leaves her without an assessment she needs after a caesarean.

explanation.issue: This tests whether you make sure a patient receives care that a record wrongly says was done, and fix the record and the system.
explanation.keyDetails: The template auto-filled the entry. No assessment was done. She is at increased risk after a caesarean.
explanation.reasoning: [C] protects her, [A] corrects the record, and [D] fixes the system. [E] corrects the record but leaves her at risk, and [B] leaves both a false record and an unassessed patient.
explanation.competing: The order of [E] and [B] is close, as neither gets her assessed. [B] ranks last because it also leaves a probably false statement in her record.

references.title: Good medical practice
references.note: Domain 4, honesty in records; Domain 3, reporting system problems.
